To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Fox-Li and beam propagation methods can be used to calculate the lower-order modes in a laser with inhomogeneous gain.
the lower-order optical modes in an inhomogeneous optical cavity can be approximated by using the Fox-Li and beam propagation methods.
the modal analysis of a resonator can be performed by employing a Fox-Li or a beam propagation method, and that this method is applicable even when the gain distribution is inhomogeneous.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the optical resonators with a gain distribution.
the modal analysis of inhomogeneously filled optical resonators.
the study of the modal properties of an optical resonators with an inhomogenous gain distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the modal analysis of an inhomogeneous optical system can be performed with the Fox-Li and beam propagation methods.
the modal analysis of inhomogeneously pumped optical resonators is not a straightforward extension of the analysis of homogeneous resonators.
a laser mode structure can be determined by a modal analysis of the gain medium, and the laser’s mode profile can then be obtained by using the Fox-Li method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modal structure of an optical resonant cavity with a gain medium is not as simple as it may first appear.
the modal analysis of inhomogeneously doped laser resonators is feasible.
we have shown how to calculate the modal properties of an optical resonant structure that is not necessarily homogeneous in gain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in principle, the beam propagation method can be used to calculate laser modes.
the lower-order transverse modes of an inhomogeneous optical cavity can be calculated by solving the scalar Helmholtz equation with a gain term.
the lower-order transverse modes of an inhomogeneously doped optical resonator can be obtained from the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a linear eigenvalue problem.
